observations.text: SP, due to a non-standardized application of the Time - Map - Ground technique, could not recognize the ground points near the flight path without assistance, with the result that the IP had to identify the checkpoints and direct the corrections. The uncorrected drift reached 15 degrees of heading and 400 feet of altitude, beyond the 10-degree and 300-foot limits. Further study of the route map and of the checkpoint selection procedure is required.

SP, due to failure to shed a secondary task when workload increased, did not maintain the Time - Map - Ground sequence and did not recognize the deviation from the first turning point, with the result that the IP took over the navigation and directed the turn. Airspeed decayed 25 knots and altitude 350 feet from the briefed values, beyond the 20-knot and 300-foot limits.

SP recognized most of the ground points near the flight path and applied the Time - Map - Ground technique within the desired standards for this Training Section, completing the map reading after the IP's verbal prompts at two turning points. Deviations remained at the 300-foot altitude and 10-degree heading limits and were recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier self-identification of the checkpoints is expected to improve.

SP applied the Time - Map - Ground technique in the correct sequence and recognized the ground points near the flight path without the IP's verbal prompts. Two secondary checkpoints were identified late, producing deviations of 200 feet in altitude and 7 degrees in heading, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP recognized confidently most of the ground points near the flight path and applied the Time - Map - Ground technique accurately and rapidly. Possible deviations from the turning points were identified in good time and the appropriate corrections were executed, with altitude held within 100 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and heading within 4 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP recognized every briefed ground point at the planned time and applied the Time - Map - Ground technique with exceptional accuracy, anticipating each turning point before the timing tolerance elapsed. Deviations were negligible, with altitude within 50 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and heading within 2 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to reading the map without reference to the elapsed time, reversed the Time - Map - Ground sequence and could not associate the observed terrain with the planned track, with the result that the IP had to identify the turning point and execute part of the correction. Heading error reached 18 degrees and altitude 450 feet from the briefed values, beyond the 10-degree and 300-foot limits.

SP, due to degraded situational awareness after the unplanned change of the route sequence, did not recognize the ground points near the flight path and did not identify the deviation from the second turning point, with the result that the IP directed the recovery of the planned track. The turning point was passed 3 NM abeam, with a 22-knot airspeed excursion and 400 feet of altitude deviation, beyond the 20-knot and 300-foot limits.

SP, due to selecting linear features that were not distinctive at the navigation altitude, did not confirm the ground points in the Time - Map - Ground order, with the result that the map reading was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts at two checkpoints. Deviations reached the 300-foot altitude and 10-degree heading limits and were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to reliance on the automated navigation solution in place of map reading, did not cross-check the ground points against the chart and the elapsed time, with the result that the deviation from the turning point was recognized only after the IP's verbal prompt. The correction was executed with delay, with heading at the 10-degree limit and altitude at 300 feet from the briefed value.

SP recognized most of the ground points and maintained the Time - Map - Ground technique within the desired standards, with minor errors recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. At two turning points the checkpoint was identified late, producing deviations of 200 feet in altitude and 8 degrees in heading. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier anticipation of the turning points is expected to improve.

SP applied the Time - Map - Ground technique in the correct sequence throughout the route and recognized confidently most of the ground points near the flight path. Possible deviations from the turning points were recognized in good time and corrected accurately, with altitude within 120 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and heading within 4 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP identified every planned ground point at or before the computed time and applied the Time - Map - Ground technique with exceptional accuracy, requiring no re-orientation at any turning point. Deviations were negligible, with altitude within 50 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and heading within 2 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to using the map without orienting it to the track, could not associate the observed terrain with the planned route and did not recognize the second turning point, with the result that the IP had to take over the navigation and direct the turn. Track error exceeded 3 NM, with 400 feet of altitude and 15 degrees of heading deviation, beyond the 300-foot and 10-degree limits.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during the leg to the second turning point, did not maintain the Time - Map - Ground sequence and did not recognize the ground points near the flight path, with the result that the IP identified the checkpoint and executed part of the correction. Airspeed and altitude deviations reached 25 knots and 500 feet, beyond the 20-knot and 300-foot limits.

SP, due to an incomplete pre-flight study of the checkpoint features, did not recognize the ground points at the planned times and did not apply the Time - Map - Ground sequence consistently, with the result that the planned track was reconstructed only after the IP's verbal prompts. Deviations were at the 300-foot altitude and 10-degree heading limits and were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to an error that went undetected because the map-to-ground cross-check was not re-established after the weather deviation, continued toward a feature that did not match the planned track, with the result that the deviation from the turning point was corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition was delayed, with heading at the 10-degree limit and airspeed 20 knots from the briefed value.

SP, due to confirming the checkpoints on the ground before referring to the elapsed time, inverted part of the Time - Map - Ground sequence and identified two secondary features late, with the result of deviations of 220 feet in altitude and 7 degrees in heading. The errors were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention.

SP, due to a lapse in which the briefed timing check was omitted under workload, did not confirm the ground points against the elapsed time and recognized the deviation from the second turning point late, with the result of a 200-foot altitude and 15-knot airspeed excursion. The deviation was corrected without IP's intervention.

SP recognized confidently most of the ground points and applied the Time - Map - Ground technique accurately and with adequate speed, holding altitude within 140 feet, airspeed within 9 knots and heading within 5 degrees. Two turning points were identified only at the computed time rather than in advance. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of the turning point features is expected to improve.

SP recognized every ground point near the flight path ahead of the computed time and applied the Time - Map - Ground technique with exceptional accuracy, executing the appropriate corrections before any track deviation could develop. Altitude was held within 50 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and heading within 2 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.
